description: The pie chart visually represents the proportional distribution of twelve distinct domains within the annotated AttrEval-GenSearch test set, with each slice corresponding to a specific category and its percentage contribution. The largest segment, colored bright blue, is “AI/NLP Research” at 24.3%, followed by the teal “Econ. & Fin.” slice at 18.4%. Two categories—“History” (yellow) and “Game&Anime” (orange)—are tied at 8.2%. “Daily Life” (light teal) accounts for 7.1%, while “Med & Health” (green) and “Science” (light blue) each make up 6.7%. “Business” (red) is slightly smaller at 5.9%, followed by “Pet & Animal” (orange-red) at 5.5% and “Law” (pink) at 5.1%. The smallest segments are “Geography” (yellow-green) at 2.7% and “Math” (dark green) at 1.2%. Each slice is clearly labeled with its category name and percentage via leader lines extending outward, and the chart uses a diverse color palette to distinguish categories. Although the caption mentions “Geography” at 3.7% and “Math” at 2.2%, the chart visually displays them as 2.7% and 1.2%, respectively, indicating a discrepancy between the caption text and the visual data. The slices are arranged in no strict order, though the largest segments are positioned roughly clockwise from the top right. The chart does not include an explicit legend, relying instead on direct labeling for clarity.
caption_used: The pie chart illustrates the domain distribution of the annotated AttrEval-GenSearch test set, encompassing twelve distinct categories. The largest category, 'AI/NLP Research,' accounts for approximately 24.3% of the dataset, followed by 'Econ. & Fin.' at 18.4%. 'History' and 'Game&Anime' are tied at 8.2%, while 'Daily Life' constitutes 7.1%. 'Med & Health' and 'Science' both represent 6.7%, with 'Business' slightly lower at 5.9%. 'Pet & Animal' and 'Law' are close in proportion, at 5.5% and 5.1%, respectively. 'Geography' and 'Math' are the smallest categories, with 'Geography' at 3.7% and 'Math' at 2.2%. Notably, 'Daily Life' has shown a consistent increase in representation compared to previous datasets, while 'Geography' has seen a slight decline.
